documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28 yo woman, elementary school teacher, here to establish. Her old PCP left practice in the spring and she'd rather not start over in a big group. No complaints today.

PMH: none. No surgeries. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father with type 2 diabetes. Mother had depression after her second pregnancy. Maternal aunt has bipolar I disorder.
SH: married, lives in Northampton. Teaches elementary school. Never smoked. Alcohol a drink or two a month at most. No drug use. Walks most evenings.
GYN: regular cycles. Last Pap 2021 at prior office, she believes normal.
ROS: negative in full.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well, pleasant. HEENT clear, TMs normal. Neck supple, thyroid normal size, no adenopathy. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd soft, nontender, no masses. Ext without edema. Skin without concerning lesions. Neuro grossly intact. Mood euthymic.

PHQ-9: 2.

A/P: Healthy adult, new to the practice.
- Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. A1c given father's diabetes.
- HIV and hep C one-time screens, she agreed.
- Records requested from prior PCP for Pap and immunization history.
- Flu shot in the fall here.
- Physical yearly.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit. She and her husband want to start trying for a baby this summer and she wants to be ready. No complaints. No meds. NKDA. Never smoker; already cutting out the occasional drink.

OB/GYN hx: G0. Cycles regular, about every 28-30 days. Pap 4/2024 normal.
FH reviewed: mother's postpartum depression after her second baby; maternal aunt with bipolar I. Father T2DM.

ROS negative. PHQ-9 1.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well-appearing. HEENT normal. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Ext no edema. Skin normal.

A/P: Preconception visit, healthy.
- Start a prenatal vitamin with iron now, 1 daily.
- No alcohol once trying. Medications and supplements: check with us first.
- Vaccines current; she'll get flu in the fall either way.
- Talked about the family history. Her mother's postpartum depression and her aunt's bipolar disorder do raise her own risk after delivery. We'll tell her OB and keep a close eye on mood after the baby comes. She appreciated knowing.
- CBC today as a baseline.
- Message us when she has a positive test and we'll get her to OB.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Isabelle, your blood count is normal, no anemia. Keep taking the prenatal vitamin.

documents.title: Positive test!
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning! Two positive home tests this weekend. First day of my last period was May 1. Feeling a little queasy in the mornings but OK. Still on the prenatal vitamin. What do I do next?

documents.title: RE: Positive test!
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations to you both! By your period you're about 4 1/2 weeks along, due date around early February. I've sent a referral to an OB group near you and they'll call to set up your first prenatal visit, usually around 8 weeks. Keep the vitamin going, no alcohol, small frequent meals help the queasiness. Call if you have heavy bleeding or bad pain. I'll let the OB know about your family history so they're watching your mood after delivery too.

documents.title: RE: Baby is here
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations! So glad it went well. Front desk will reach out for a postpartum visit with me around 6 weeks. In the meantime sleep whenever you can, and please call or text me directly any time, day or night, if your mood or sleep feel off, even if it seems small.

events.reason: Husband calling, patient confused and not sleeping

documents.title: Urgent call from husband
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Husband called my cell. Isabelle has barely slept for several days, was up all night pacing and muttering, and keeps saying someone wants to hurt the baby. He says she doesn't seem to know what day it is. No weapons in the home. Baby is with him and safe.

This sounds like postpartum psychosis until proven otherwise. Told him to take her to the ED now, not to leave her alone with the baby, and to call 911 if she won't go or tries to leave. Called ahead to the ED and gave her history and the family history. He's driving her in.

events.reason: Insomnia, paranoid thoughts, agitation 10 days postpartum

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department, community hospital
Seen 02/13/2026

CC: not sleeping, paranoid, agitated; 10 days postpartum.

HPI: 31 yo G1P1, ten days after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and last seen by OB in January for a prenatal visit. Husband brought her in at her PCP's direction. Over the past several days she has hardly slept, and he has found her talking to herself. She has been insisting that someone is trying to harm their baby and has grown more and more agitated at home. Patient herself gives little history.

PMH: uncomplicated first pregnancy, no psychiatric history. Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with postpartum depression; maternal aunt with bipolar I; father with type 2 diabetes.
SH: teacher, on maternity leave. Never smoker; no alcohol in pregnancy or since delivery.

Exam: vitals within normal limits. Disheveled. Appears to be responding to internal stimuli. Oriented to person only, not to time or place. No focal neurologic findings. Breasts soft, uterus firm and nontender below umbilicus.

Labs: Hgb 12.5, WBC 7.0, platelets 250. TSH 2.5. Urinalysis normal.

MDM: acute psychosis in the early postpartum period with a family history of bipolar disorder; labs do not suggest a medical cause. Psychiatric emergency. Psychiatry consulted in the ED and recommended admission.

Disposition: admitted to inpatient psychiatry.
Dx: postpartum psychosis.

Emergency Medicine

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Psychiatry Discharge Summary
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Inpatient Psychiatry, community hospital
Admitted 02/13/2026, discharged 02/20/2026

Diagnosis: postpartum psychosis.
Allergies: NKDA.

Course: 31 yo woman admitted from the ED 10 days after her first delivery with several days of insomnia, paranoid fears about harm coming to her infant, agitation and disorientation. ED labs (CBC, TSH, UA) unremarkable. She was started on olanzapine 5 mg at bedtime, raised to 10 mg on hospital day 3. Sleep was restored by day 4 and the delusional fears had cleared by day 6. At discharge she was calm, fully oriented and organized, with insight into the episode. At no time did she voice thoughts of harming herself or her baby.

Feeding: she expressed milk with a hospital-grade pump throughout the stay and her husband brought it home, so the infant remained on breast milk alone. Lactation saw her twice. Olanzapine is considered compatible with breastfeeding; the infant's pediatrician has been told to watch for sleepiness.

Discharge medications:
- olanzapine 10 mg at bedtime
- prenatal vitamin with iron daily

Discharge plan: home with husband; family to help with nights so she gets an unbroken stretch of sleep. Outpatient perinatal psychiatry 02/26. PCP visit within the week. Warning signs reviewed with both of them.

Psychiatry

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with husband and the baby, 3 days after discharge from inpatient psychiatry (2/13-2/20) for postpartum psychosis. Discharge summary reviewed this morning.

She's quiet but herself. Sleeping 5-6 hours in a row; her husband and family are covering the night feeds with pumped milk and she nurses during the day. Taking olanzapine 10 mg at night without problems. No voices, no worries about the baby being harmed. Remembers the episode in pieces and is upset about it. No thoughts of hurting herself or the baby. Husband agrees she is back to baseline.

Meds: olanzapine 10 mg qhs (psychiatry), prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Calm, well-groomed, good eye contact, speech normal, thought process linear, no evidence of psychosis. Oriented x3. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Breasts not examined today, no complaints.

A/P:
1. Postpartum psychosis, resolved on olanzapine. Continue 10 mg qhs as prescribed by psychiatry; first outpatient psychiatry visit Thursday. Protecting sleep is the most important thing right now; the family plan is solid.
2. Breastfeeding, going well with pumping overnight.
3. Safety: she and husband know to call me or go to the ED for any return of sleeplessness, odd thoughts, or worries about the baby.
Postpartum visit with me as planned in mid-March. I'll call her next week.

events.reason: Right breast pain, redness and fever

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth 4 times daily for 10 days

documents.title: Obstetrics: Postpartum Problem Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Obstetrics & Gynecology, outside group
Date of service: 02/24/2026

RE: Isabelle Murphy, DOB 08/27/1994

Seen 3 weeks after her vaginal delivery, and recently home from an inpatient stay for postpartum psychosis. She is exclusively breastfeeding. For two days her right breast has been increasingly sore, swollen and red, worst in the upper outer part, with chills and fever at home. She says the baby has started "biting" at the breast and she has a crack on the right nipple.

Medications: olanzapine 10 mg at bedtime, prenatal vitamin with iron. NKDA.

T 38.7 C, HR 96.
Right breast: erythema and induration of the upper outer quadrant, tender to touch. No fluctuance. No nipple discharge. Fissure at the right nipple. Left breast normal.

Assessment: lactational mastitis, right breast.
Plan:
- Cephalexin 500 mg four times daily x 10 days; safe with breastfeeding.
- Keep nursing or pumping from the right side; ibuprofen as needed for pain and fever.
- Lactation follow-up for latch and the nipple.
- Call for worsening redness, a fluctuant area, or fever beyond 48 hours on antibiotics.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Perinatal Psychiatry: Follow-up Letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Perinatal Psychiatry, outside clinic
Date of service: 02/26/2026

Dear Doctor,
I saw Ms. Murphy for her first outpatient visit after her admission for postpartum psychosis. She has had no return of psychotic symptoms since discharge. Her family is protecting her sleep and she is getting a solid 5-6 hours most nights. Tolerating olanzapine. She is being treated with cephalexin for right mastitis by her OB.

Mental status: calm, linear, no delusions or perceptual disturbance, no suicidal or infanticidal thoughts.

Plan: continue olanzapine 10 mg at bedtime. Follow-up every 4-8 weeks. Given her history we will be watching closely for postpartum depression over the coming weeks and would value your screening at her postpartum visit.

Perinatal Psychiatry

documents.title: Postpartum Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Postpartum visit, about 5 1/2 weeks after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Since then: ED and inpatient psychiatry 2/13-2/20 for postpartum psychosis, on olanzapine; right lactational mastitis 2/24 treated by OB with cephalexin, course done.

Today she says she's been feeling low for a couple of weeks. Can't sleep even when the baby is down and someone else has the night shift. Doesn't care about things she used to love, reading, walks, texting friends. Feels guilty a lot, that she isn't a good enough mother and "missed" the first weeks. Hard to focus, tired most of the day. Not hungry; thinks she's down about 5 lb since the delivery. No thoughts of hurting herself or the baby, no thoughts of being better off dead. No voices, no suspicious or strange thoughts; husband (here today) agrees. Breast is fine now, no fever since the first days of antibiotics. Nursing by day, pumped milk at night.

Meds: olanzapine 10 mg qhs (psychiatry), prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

PHQ-9 17, item 9 = 0.

Exam: vitals normal. Alert, cooperative, thought process linear and goal-directed, no psychotic features. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Breasts: no erythema, induration or tenderness; nipples healed. Ext no edema.

A/P:
1. Postpartum depression, moderately severe. New. Called her perinatal psychiatrist from the room; we agreed to start sertraline with the olanzapine as cover. Sertraline 50 mg tabs, 1/2 tab daily x 1 week then 1 tab. Compatible with breastfeeding. Referral to a perinatal therapist. Safety plan written out with both of them; she can reach me directly any hour.
2. Postpartum psychosis, in remission. Continue olanzapine 10 mg qhs per psychiatry. Any sleeplessness or odd thinking: call same day.
3. Mastitis right breast, resolved.
4. TSH today; ED value was normal but rechecking with new depression postpartum.
RN call in a week, see me in 4 weeks.

documents.title: Thyroid test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Morning Isabelle, your thyroid test from Friday is normal, same as in the hospital. So thyroid isn't behind how you've been feeling. Keep going with the sertraline and let me know how the first week goes.

documents.title: RN Check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt one week into sertraline. Taking 1/2 tab daily, steps up to a whole tab tomorrow. Sleeping about the same. Denies thoughts of self-harm or harming baby, no unusual thoughts. Therapist's office called her, intake 4/14. Has f/u with PCP 4/10. Reviewed when to call. Routed to PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: Postpartum Depression
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
4 weeks on sertraline, 3 weeks at 50 mg. "Some better days now." Falling asleep more easily; still wakes early some mornings. Enjoying walks with the baby again. Guilt less constant. Concentration still patchy. Eating more. No SI, no thoughts of harming the baby, no psychotic symptoms. Therapy intake next week.

Meds: sertraline 50 mg daily, olanzapine 10 mg qhs, prenatal vitamin.

PHQ-9 12 (was 17).

Exam: brighter, smiles appropriately, linear. Vitals fine.

A/P: Postpartum depression, improving on sertraline 50. Early in the response; stay at 50 for now, psychiatry agrees. Psychosis remains in remission on olanzapine. Return 6 weeks, sooner if needed.

Perinatal Psychiatry, outside clinic
Date of service: 04/21/2026

Dear Doctor,
Follow-up for Ms. Murphy. No psychotic symptoms since February. Depression clearly lifting on the sertraline you started; she has begun weekly CBT. Sleep fair. No mood elevation, no decreased need for sleep.

Current medications: olanzapine 10 mg at bedtime, sertraline 50 mg daily, prenatal vitamin.

Plan: continue both at current doses. Since she is now about 2 months on olanzapine, could you check a fasting lipid panel, A1c and metabolic panel at her next visit with you? Next visit here in about 3 months.

Perinatal Psychiatry

documents.title: Follow-up: Mood
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came fasting for the labs psychiatry asked for. Mood a lot better. Sleeping through when it's her night off, falls back asleep after feeds. Laughing again, seeing friends. Some days still flat. Likes therapy. Taking sertraline and olanzapine every day. No SI, no psychotic symptoms, no stretches of unusual energy or not needing sleep.

PHQ-9 7.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight 67.0, continuing to come down since delivery. Bright affect, linear.

1. Postpartum depression, improving. Sertraline 50 mg, no change.
2. Postpartum psychosis, in remission on olanzapine 10 mg. Metabolic labs today: lipids, A1c, CMP. Will forward to psychiatry.
Next visit 2 months.

Meds: sertraline 50 mg daily, olanzapine 10 mg qhs, prenatal vitamin.

PHQ-9 4.

Exam: vitals fine, weight 66.4. Euthymic, full range of affect.

A/P: Postpartum depression, much improved, PHQ-9 down from 17 to 4. Continue sertraline; we'll talk about how long to stay on it once she's been well for 6 months or so. Psychosis remains in remission; olanzapine plan per psychiatry, she sees them next week. Next visit in 2 months, physical is due too.

Date of service: 07/22/2026

Dear Doctor,
Ms. Murphy continues to do well. Her psychosis has stayed in full remission since February and her depression has largely resolved. Sleep and mood steady; no hypomanic features. Thank you for the metabolic labs in May, which were normal.
